#### About the Barbara Hepworth Museum

[Barbara Hepworth](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/dame-barbara-hepworth-1274) first came to live in Cornwall with her husband [Ben Nicholson](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/ben-nicholson-om-1702) and their young family at the outbreak of war in 1939. She lived and worked in Trewyn Studio – now the Barbara Hepworth Museum – from 1949 until her death in 1975.

'Finding Trewyn Studio was a sort of magic’, wrote Hepworth. ‘Here was a studio, a yard and garden where I could work in open air and space'.

Most of the bronzes are in the positions in which the artist herself placed them. The garden itself was laid out by Barbara Hepworth with help from a friend, the composer Priaulx Rainier.

## Getting Here

### Address

Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden 
Barnoon Hill 
St Ives 
Cornwall TR26 1AD

### Directions

[Walk](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/dir//Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden,+Barnoon Hill,+St Ives,+Cornwall TR26 1AD,+United+Kingdom/data=!4m2!4m1!3e2) [Cycle](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/dir//Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden,+Barnoon Hill,+St Ives,+Cornwall TR26 1AD,+United+Kingdom/data=!4m2!4m1!3e1) [Ride](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/dir//Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden,+Barnoon Hill,+St Ives,+Cornwall TR26 1AD,+United+Kingdom/data=!4m2!4m1!3e3) [Drive](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/dir//Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden,+Barnoon Hill,+St Ives,+Cornwall TR26 1AD,+United+Kingdom/data=!4m2!4m1!3e0)

#### By foot

The gallery and museum are within walking distance of St Ives town centre and Porthmeor beach.

#### By Bicycle

There is a covered bicycle rack at the rear of Tate St Ives, by Barnoon car park. Property is left at the owner's risk. The entrance to the Hepworth Museum is a short walk down Barnoon Hill towards the town.

#### By Bus

There are regular local bus services to and from St Ives.

[Traveline - local public transport information](https://www.travelinesw.com/)

#### By train

A frequent rail service operates between London Paddington and St Ives via Reading, Exeter, Plymouth, Bodmin, Truro, St Erth and Penzance. A local train service operates from St Erth to St Ives. For train times and booking see:

[National Rail Enquiries](http://www.nationalrail.co.uk/) or call 08457 000 125[First Great Western](http://www.firstgreatwestern.co.uk/)

#### By coach

There are daily National Express coach services from Victoria Coach Station, London. These services travel via Heathrow, Plymouth, Liskeard, St Austell, Truro, Redruth, Camborne, St Ives and Penzance – stopping at most small towns en route.

[National Express](http://www.nationalexpress.com/home.aspx)

#### By car

St Ives is an historic fishing town with naturally narrow, largely car-free streets. While it’s only a 15–20 minute drive from the A30, driving can be stressful and parking is limited, so it's best to leave the car behind.

The St Erth Park and Ride is a popular option, letting you take in the scenic St Ives Bay train line, or you can park at Trenwith car park and taking the shuttle bus into town. If you plan to drive into St Ives, please plan ahead by visiting the [Cornwall Council website](https://www.cornwall.gov.uk/transport-parking-and-streets/parking/cornwall-council-car-parks/council-car-parks-in-st-ives-including-carbis-bay/).

Please note: The Hepworth Museum does not have a car park.

#### By shuttle bus

A shuttle bus service runs throughout the year between the [Trenwith Coach and Car Park](https://www.cornwall.gov.uk/transport-parking-and-streets/parking/cornwall-council-car-parks/trenwith-st-ives-tr26-1dd/) and the town centre, which is a five minute walk from Tate St Ives. Call St Ives Tourist Information on +44 (0)1736 796297 for details.

#### By park and ride

A park and ride service operates from St Erth train station, offering a scenic 10 minute journey into St Ives on the St Ives bay line. Visit [Great Scenic Railways for more information](https://greatscenicrailways.co.uk/stations/st-erth-park-and-ride/).

#### By air

The nearest airport is in Newquay, the regional commercial airport for Cornwall.

[Newquay Airport](https://www.cornwallairportnewquay.com/)

### Entrance

There are steps and uneven surfaces that make access difficult. For this reason manual wheelchair access is by prior appointment only.

To book call [+44 (0)173 679 6226](tel:+44(0)1736796226).

Mobility scooters are not permitted.

### Wheelchair provision

Manual wheelchairs available for booking.

To book a manual wheelchair for your visit call [+44 (0)1736 796 226](tel:+4401736796226) 
or email [visiting.stives@tate.org.uk](mailto:visiting.stives@tate.org.uk)

Bookings should be made at least 24 hours before visiting.

### Assistance Dogs

We welcome guide dogs, hearing dogs and assistance dogs. Drinking bowls are available – just ask a member of staff.

### Visual story

Our step-by-step visual and written guide can help you plan your visit.

[Go to the visual story](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives/barbara-hepworth-museum-and-sculpture-garden/visual-story)

### Story player

You can explore the museum and Barbara Hepworth's life and work through our [story player](https://www.tate.org.uk/story-player/barbara-hepworth-museum).

Story players are a collection of audio resources. They can guide you through your visit, or you can enjoy them online wherever you are.

[Listen to the story player](https://www.tate.org.uk/story-player/barbara-hepworth-museum)

### Contact us

Email [visiting.stives@tate.org.uk](mailto:visiting.stives@tate.org.uk)

Call [+44 (0)173 679 6226](tel:+44(0)1736796226)
